summary: Node 05 regex requires a trailing period; three sutras merged into the preceding chunk
description:
NOT missing text. The Johnston edition is complete and correct. Three sutra
boundaries were not detected, so each of those sutras was absorbed into the
chunk before it.

## Cause

chunking/hinduism/yoga-sutras-book-0*.toml uses

    regex-section-split  '(?:^|\s)(\d+)\.\s'

which requires a period after the number. The sacred-texts pages omit it in
exactly three places:

    book 02   "...or the links of manacles. 5 The darkness of ignorance is:..."
    book 02   "...firmly and steadfastly on his feet. 48 The fruit of right poise..."
    book 03   "...'the vision and the faculty divine.' 34 By perfectly concentrated..."

Everywhere else the source writes "N. ".

## Effect — a citation-integrity defect

    hinduism.yoga-sutras-book-02.004   label "Sutra 4"    contains sutras 4 + 5
    hinduism.yoga-sutras-book-02.046   label "Sutra 47"   contains sutras 47 + 48
    hinduism.yoga-sutras-book-03.033   label "Sutra 33"   contains sutras 33 + 34

192 chunks against a 195-sutra canon. AGENTS.md: "a chunk id is a promise that
a specific passage says a specific thing." Three ids currently deliver two
sutras while naming one.

No text is lost, and every other chunk is correct.

## Fix is not free — re-chunking renumbers ids

Chunk ids are file-ordinal, labels are sutra-number, and they have already
diverged (book-02 file 046.toml is labelled "Sutra 47"; the last file, 053,
is "Sutra 55"). Splitting the three merged chunks renumbers everything after
them:

    book 02   chunks 004-053 shift   (50 chunks)
    book 03   chunks 033-054 shift   (22 chunks)

That invalidates every staged_tag, staged_edge and review_action keyed to
those ids — including the 696 edge verdicts queued in this session and the
already-applied tag decisions for books 02 and 03.

## Options

1. Widen the regex to '(?:^|\s)(\d+)\.?\s(?=[A-Z])' and re-chunk books 02 and
   03, then re-run nodes 07, 09, 10, 12, 13 for them and re-review. Correct,
   and expensive: it discards reviewed work for two of four books.
2. Patch the three chunk files by hand — split each into two, renumber, and
   migrate the affected staged_* rows. Cheaper, but hand-edited corpus output
   contradicts "corpus/*.toml is generated".
3. Ship as-is and correct only the three section labels to "Sutra 4-5",
   "Sutra 47-48", "Sutra 33-34", so the id stops over-promising. No
   renumbering, no lost review, citations become honest rather than precise.
4. Re-chunk before applying the queues, accepting the loss of the yoga edge
   review for books 02 and 03 (about 350 of 696 edges).

Option 3 is the only one that costs nothing already done; option 1 is the only
one that ends with 195 addressable sutras. The decision belongs to the corpus
owner.

## Why it survived to a post-hoc review

Nothing between nodes 05 and 14 counts emitted units against the source's own
numbering. Node 05's own gate is that the config parses and produces chunks;
193 vs 195 is invisible to it. Added as a node 05 failure mode.

resolution.note: Fix landed in ccd6f18c; verified 195/195 with labels aligned 1:1 and the three named boundaries opening their own chunks. This commit adds the standing guard that was missing.
